meta.description: Mark and remove PCR/optical duplicates using samtools fixmate and markdup. Use when preparing alignments for variant calling or when duplicate reads would bias analysis. Not for RNA-seq, amplicon or UMI libraries (see the decision table).
meta.audit_kind: final-pass Phase 2 fresh audit; every prior report input was re-run as regression coverage, with two new inputs
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All reported counts were asserted from this audit's logs; no identifiers, outcomes, or performance claims were fabricated.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill processes alignment files and gives no individual diagnosis or treatment recommendation.

methodological_ground.detail: The decision table and executable assay gate correctly refuse RNA-seq and UMI workflows for ordinary markdup; UMI workflows use the documented dedicated tools.

code_usability.detail: The shipped scripts and documented CLI paths completed with asserted BAM counts, indexes, metrics, or expected failure messages in the supplied WSL environment.

functional_suitability.note: The standard, UMI-aware, alternative-marker, and assay-boundary paths are all present and the exercised commands match their stated purpose.

reliability.note: Scripts use pipefail, temporary paths, count checks, and explicit failure exits; the remaining gap is real HiFi amplicon validation for pbmarkdup.

performance_context.note: The 291-line SKILL.md delegates detailed branches to focused references and executable scripts, though several tool choices still require reading a reference.

agent_usability.note: Assay-first routing, verbatim errors, version checks, and output checks make the workflow clear; alternative environment installation is intentionally left to the user environment.

human_usability.note: Natural triggers and the concise usage guide are strong; the breadth of assay choices still requires the decision table.

security.note: No credentials, eval/exec, destructive broad deletion, or sensitive-data handling are present; CLI path arguments rely on the called tools' normal filesystem semantics.

maintainability.note: References separate UMI, alternative-marker, and pysam concerns, while scripts isolate repeatable workflows and expose checkable counts.

agent_specific.note: The trigger, progressive disclosure, related skills, assay escape hatches, seeded UMI behavior, and temporary-output handling are strong; pbmarkdup remains real-data unverified.

inputs.label: Standard paired-end duplicate workflow
inputs.note: The five-step samtools workflow, pysam helper, rate helper, and Picard independent marker all matched the 100-read planted truth.

inputs.note: The shipped pipeline produced a 100-read marked BAM and stats; unset assay and detected RNA inputs exited 2 without outputs, while the explicit override completed.

assertions.note: The run exited 2 and left neither BAM nor stats.

inputs.label: Common errors and rerun behavior
inputs.note: Three representative Common Errors rows exactly matched tool output; re-marking with -c restored the planted 100 duplicate flags.

assertions.text: Queryname-sorted input to markdup produces the documented error.

assertions.text: Re-marking with -c succeeds and yields the expected flags.
assertions.note: The cleared rerun flagged 100 reads.

assertions.text: The error paths terminate rather than silently marking incorrect data.
assertions.note: Each asserted misuse exited non-zero.

inputs.label: PacBio HiFi amplicon command
inputs.note: This new deterministic synthetic HiFi input confirmed flags and removal behavior, but it cannot establish performance on a real HiFi amplicon library.
inputs.execution_note: phase2_audit.sh INPUT 7 with make_hifi.py; phase2_audit.log records 12 duplicate flags from 60 reads and 48 reads after --rmdup.

assertions.text: The documented pbmarkdup command accepts an unaligned PacBio-style BAM.
assertions.note: pbmarkdup completed on the seeded input.

assertions.text: pbmarkdup flags the deterministic planted duplicates.
assertions.note: It flagged 12 of 60 reads.

assertions.text: pbmarkdup --rmdup removes the flagged records.
assertions.note: The removal output held 48 reads.

assertions.text: The synthetic input is reproducible and clearly labeled as synthetic.
assertions.note: make_hifi.py fixes the random seed and documents its 12-read truth.

assertions.text: The PacBio HiFi amplicon claim is validated on a real public amplicon library.
assertions.note: No small real public HiFi amplicon BAM or FASTQ is available in the audit environment.

key_strengths: Every prior audit input family was re-run on the fixed tip, with checked BAM counts, indexes, metrics, or expected error text.
The shipped pipeline now prevents wrong-assay use both from the declared assay and from an RNA-seq heuristic, while keeping an explicit override.
UMI branches are reproducible through a random seed and correctly separate single-strand from duplex consensus.
Alternative marker coverage includes independent duplicate counts, Picard UMI-aware marking, and mapDamage rescaling.

recommendations.title: Validate pbmarkdup on real HiFi amplicon data
recommendations.problem: The documented pbmarkdup command was verified only with a deterministic synthetic unaligned HiFi-style BAM. Its behavior on a real HiFi amplicon BAM or FASTQ remains unobserved.
recommendations.root_cause: The audit environment has no small public HiFi amplicon dataset and the checkpoint records no suitable source.
recommendations.fix: When a public HiFi amplicon BAM or FASTQ under 50 MB is available, run the documented command and assert flag or removal behavior against independently inspected duplicate families.
